title: Installation: packages, containers and the managed service

videos.script: There are three ways to get a PostgreSQL server, and they look like three ways to do the same thing. {{three}} A package puts the server on a machine you run. A container puts it in a box on a machine you run. A managed service puts it on a machine somebody else runs, and hands you an address. {{address}} The difference is not the server. It is the same program in all three. The difference is who can open its files, who restarts it, and who gets the phone call when it stops. {{who}} This lesson builds the one you will use for the rest of the course: a virtual machine with Ubuntu, and PostgreSQL from Ubuntu's own packages. {{vm}} It is a server you own completely. You can read its configuration, fill its disk and break it on purpose. A managed service will never let you do any of that, and that is exactly why it cannot teach you what it hides. {{break}} By the end you will have a running cluster, a role with your name on it, and a first look at what the installer did to the machine. {{title}}
